chunks: Musa, the Prophet (peace be upon him), passed by the glens of Al-Rawha upon a red camel whose halter was made of palm fibres. Upon him were two Qatwani cloaks, and he was saying: 'Here I am, O Benevolent One! Here I am!'
He said: And Yunus ibn Matta passed by the glens of Al-Rawha, and he was saying: 'Here I am, O Remover of grievous anguish! Here I am!'
He said: And Isa ibn Maryam passed by the glens of Al-Rawha, and he was saying: 'Here I am, Your servant, son of Your maidservant! Here I am!'
And Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) passed by the glens of Al-Rawha, and he was saying: 'Here I am, O Possessor of the Lofty Ascents! Here I am!'

key_terms.ذَا الْمَعَارِجِ: Possessor of the Lofty Ascents — a Quranic epithet of God (cf. Surah al-Ma'arij 70:3)
key_terms.صِفَاحِ الرَّوْحَاءِ: The glens/plains of Al-Rawha — a geographical location on the Hajj route between Medina and Mecca
key_terms.قَطَوَانِيَّتَانِ: Qatwani — a type of coarse woollen cloak associated with the city of Qatwana, representing prophetic simplicity and asceticism
key_terms.كَشَّافَ الْكُرَبِ الْعِظَامِ: Remover of grievous anguish — a divine attribute invoked by Yunus, recalling his rescue from the whale
key_terms.لَبَّيْكَ: Talbiyya — the pilgrim's response 'Here I am' addressed to God; the central call of Hajj

ai.seo_question: What talbiyya (Labbayk) did the prophets Musa, Yunus, Isa, and Muhammad recite during Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith narrated from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (a.s.) presents a vivid scene of four great prophets — Musa, Yunus, Isa, and Muhammad — all performing the talbiyya (the pilgrim's call of 'Labbayk') at the same geographical location of Al-Rawha on their way to Hajj. Each prophet's talbiyya uniquely reflects his spiritual experience and understanding of God: Musa calls upon God's generosity, Yunus upon His power to relieve suffering, Isa emphasizes his servanthood and human origin, and Muhammad addresses God with the epithet of 'the Lofty Ascents' (Dhu al-Ma'arij). The hadith establishes the ancient institution of Hajj as a universal rite performed by all prophets, and highlights that each prophet had a distinct but equally valid way of expressing devotion in the divine call.
